themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in Central Harlem spiked to 5 reports THIS WEEK, a 233% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.5 complaints per week, signaling a sudden and concentrated escalation in open drug use or dealing that demands immediate investigation into whether this represents a new trafficking pattern or enforcement gap.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% spike, z-score: 3.5)
Statistically significant anomaly meets high-severity threshold
Most recent spike data available in dataset, indicating active/ongoing concern
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and community residents about whether this reflects new supply flows or enforcement changes in the district
Map complaint locations to identify whether spike is geographically concentrated (specific blocks/parks) or dispersed across CD 110

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints in Central Harlem surged to 5 reports last week, a 471% jump over the 8-week baseline of 0.9 complaints weekly, suggesting either organized tree removal activity, development-related damage, or a new wave of vandalism that threatens the district's green infrastructure.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (471% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Spike occurred last week—second-most recent signal in dataset
Three active ULURP applications (254 W 124th St, One45, 2395 Frederick Douglass Blvd) could be connected to construction-related damage
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaint addresses with DOB permit filings (487 total filings, 413 alterations in last 90 days) to determine if development activity is triggering tree damage
Contact Parks Department to assess whether spike reflects organized illegal removal or enforcement against developers violating tree protection rules

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaint Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (likely Uber/Lyft/app-based services) jumped to 6 reports last week, a 269% increase over the 8-week baseline of 1.6 weekly complaints, indicating either a surge in illegal or unsafe ride-hailing operations, or enforcement crackdown that residents are reporting.
evidence: 6 for-hire vehicle complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score: 4.41)
Spike is recent (last week) but not as immediate as drug activity spike (this week)
Aligns with broader noise/street complaints (1,368 street noise complaints in 90-day window)
reporting_angles: Identify complaint types (illegal pickups, unsafe driving, congestion, traffic violations) to understand specific resident grievances
Report on TLC enforcement activity and whether the spike reflects increased monitoring or genuine rise in unregulated vehicles

themes_detail.label: Water System Failure Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints peaked at 26 reports three weeks ago, a 236% spike over the 8-week baseline of 7.8 weekly complaints, indicating either a localized infrastructure failure (main break, pump issue) or building-level water delivery crisis affecting multiple residents in Central Harlem.
evidence: 26 water system complaints three weeks ago vs. 7.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (236% spike, z-score: 6.48—highest z-score in dataset)
Spike is 3 weeks old (more dated than drug/tree/vehicle spikes), but highest statistical severity overall
Converges with high baseline of heat/hot water complaints (3,396 total over 90 days) and plumbing spike (700% last week)
reporting_angles: Investigate DEP records for main breaks, water main work, or system outages in CD 110 around the 3-week-ago timeframe; cross-check with 311 complaint locations
Interview residents in affected buildings to determine if water crisis has been resolved or if it's an ongoing hardship; tie to Dept. of Environmental Protection capital budget requests (pending)

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Crisis in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked dramatically to 3 reports two weeks ago, a 700% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.4 weekly complaints, suggesting either a widespread water infrastructure problem, aging building failures, or a cluster of building code violations affecting multiple properties in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 plumbing complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42—second-highest z-score)
Directly converges with water system spike (three weeks ago) and broader heat/hot water crisis (3,396 complaints in 90 days), suggesting interconnected infrastructure failure
Community Board budget data shows repeated requests for DEP capital upgrades—ongoing, unsolved problem
reporting_angles: Investigate whether plumbing spike is concentrated in specific buildings or blocks; cross-reference with DOB violation data and HPD housing complaints
Report on whether landlords are making emergency repairs or if residents are facing prolonged outages; connect to broader housing quality and habitability story
